findings.reason: without an open followup the roadmap cannot dispatch the section that was just authorised, which is exactly the defect the author accepted and fixed for §13 by adding f-tchhab-013.
findings.text: §5 was un-deferred to `implementable` on 2026-11-10, but every open followup names a different section (f-tchhab-008 §8, f-tchhab-011 §11, f-tchhab-012 §12, f-tchhab-013 §13); the only followup whose prompt invokes §5, f-tchhab-003, is `resolved` and carries an outcome, so the roadmap has no invocation that reaches §5

findings.reason: the node can execute its deliverable correctly and still fail its gate, or pass because §11's 148 GB index reclaim landed on 2026-11-10 without §5 removing anything; either way the measure is not attributable to this node's action, so the criterion must be a before/after delta the run's own log establishes.
findings.text: the closing criterion "the combined size of the four stores is at least 100 GB lower than the §1 figures" has already been run and already failed: f-tchhab-003 records that the 2026-10-16 reclaim "freed 162.6 GB and took no worktree… It did not bring the four stores 100 GB below §1, because other projects' report stores grew past it", and f-tchhab-004 records `crew/reports` at 187 GB, mostly imas-efit's 139 GB and nova's 35 GB, which the plan itself says its coordinators own

findings.reason: the two done-when clauses that cover those groups ("the crew home holds no redirection-named directory", "git status --porcelain lists none of the seven files") hold before the node touches anything and therefore cannot fail, and a node told to remove "the 18" from a set of 106 has no way to identify which trees were meant.
findings.text: two of the three removal groups are already gone from the live tree and the third is sized against a stale count: `~/.config/reckon/crew` holds no redirection-named directory (0 of its 75 entries carry a space), none of `9`, `14`, `16`, `42`, `47`, `192`, `head` exists at `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon`, and `git worktree list` at that checkout reports 106 worktrees against the "18 clean worktrees" the deliverable names

findings.reason: the node already runs the report-only pass first, so the control is one sentence away (that pass removes nothing and the store sizes are unchanged after it), and without it nothing in the record shows the `--apply` pass stayed inside the set it listed.
findings.text: §5 declares no negative control for an irreversible destructive pass; "the removal listing is in the log before the first removal line" is an ordering check that holds however the removal behaves
